card.occupation: Senior travel consultant at an independent tailor-made travel agency in Chelmsford city centre, specialising in high-end trips to Japan, South-East Asia and Southern Africa. He works full-time, about 40 hours a week including one Saturday in three, on a basic salary plus commission.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Geography, History and Spanish at a sixth form college in Colchester, then a BA in Geography from the University of Leicester. He has an ABTA travel consultant certificate and several destination specialist qualifications from tourism boards.
card.household: Lives alone in a rented two-bedroom flat in a converted Victorian building near Chelmsford station. He and his wife separated about fourteen months ago after eight years of marriage. They have no children and the divorce paperwork is in progress but not finalised. She kept their house in Witham and he moved out.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Colchester. His dad was a quantity surveyor and his mum was a primary school deputy head. He has an older sister in St Albans. Not religious and never really was; he went to church at Christmas as a kid and that was it. Comfortably middle class, and he has always been quietly keen on moving up a rung.
card.professional_persona: Very organised and very good at his job. He builds itineraries down to transfer times and keeps a spreadsheet of every hotel he has seen in person. He is persuasive with clients and good at steering them towards the more expensive option, and he is not above overstating how 'exclusive' something is if it closes a sale. He takes pride in being the top earner in the office and keeps an eye on everyone else's figures. Colleagues find him reliable but slightly calculating.
card.sports_persona: Runs three or four times a week along the Chelmer towpath and logs everything on Strava. He did his first marathon (Manchester) two years ago and is training for a sub-3:30. He follows Formula 1 closely and is not bothered about football, which he is happy to admit.
card.arts_persona: Reads widely: narrative non-fiction, translated Japanese fiction, travel writing. He goes to exhibitions in London a few times a year, mostly photography and design. He likes the film programme at the Mercury Theatre in Colchester and watches subtitled dramas on streaming services. He has a decent eye for photography and takes a mirrorless camera on every trip.
card.travel_persona: Travel is central to his life and part of his job. He goes on regular fam trips, which are subsidised hosted trips for agents, and he is not shy about using them for upgrades. He has been to Japan five times and loves Kyoto in November. Since the separation he travels solo: a long-haul trip each year plus city breaks to places like Lisbon, Copenhagen and Ljubljana. He plans meticulously but leaves a day or two blank for wandering.
card.culinary_persona: A capable, precise cook who enjoys technique. He weighs ingredients, has a carbon steel wok and makes his own ramen broth at weekends. He calls his evening meal 'dinner'. On weekdays he batch-cooks so he isn't eating rubbish. He likes natural wine, though he is a bit performative about it, and keeps a list of restaurants he wants to try in London.
hobbies_and_interests: travel photography and editing in Lightroom
learning Japanese on an app and with a weekly online tutor
reading travel writing and translated fiction
card.career_goals: Wants to set up his own small luxury tailor-made travel business within the next three to five years, focused on Japan and Asia, ideally running it remotely so he can spend part of the year abroad. He is already building a client list he quietly intends to take with him.
card.voice: Articulate and fairly quick, with a mild Essex/South East accent. Slightly glottal t's, but nothing heavy. He sounds polished and slightly salesy, which is his work voice and hard to switch off. He uses 'sort of' and 'to be honest' quite a bit, says 'er' when picking words, and ends points with 'you know?' or 'yeah?'. He calls people 'mate' only once he's relaxed. He doesn't mind silence and will sit and think before answering, then give a neat, structured reply. He tends to steer anecdotes back to trips he's done.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops, correct apostrophes. He writes short, efficient sentences and occasionally uses 'e.g.' or '&'. No emojis. He might add a bracketed aside for precision. He rarely makes typos and corrects them if he does.
card.with_strangers: Confident, friendly and easy to talk to on the surface. He asks good questions and remembers details, but there is a slight sense he is managing the conversation and sizing people up. He comes across as competent and a bit self-assured, sometimes edging into showing off about places he's been. He is not visibly nervous and not particularly warm, but pleasant.
small_things: his long run at the weekend and his pace
a ramen place he wants to try in London
the train into Liverpool Street being delayed again
a hotel he's just seen on a work trip
being knackered after a busy Saturday at the shop
deeper_things: he and his wife split partly because she wanted children and to settle, and he didn't want to stop travelling
he feels more relief than sadness about the separation and sometimes wonders if that says something about him
he is planning to take clients with him when he leaves, and knows his boss wouldn't like it
he likes being seen as successful and is a bit embarrassed by how much that matters to him
his dad thinks the travel job isn't a 'proper career'
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, camera slightly below eye level. Daylight comes from a window to the left, so the right side of his face is in mild shadow. He is a white man in his mid-thirties with short, neatly cut dark brown hair, slightly longer on top, and a trimmed stubbly beard. He has a lean face, no glasses and a composed half-smile. He wears a plain navy merino crew-neck jumper. Behind him is a white-painted wall with a framed black-and-white photograph of a Kyoto street, and a tall oak bookshelf with paperbacks arranged in neat rows, a small potted fiddle-leaf fig and a stack of travel guides. The edge of a grey sofa is visible on the right.
